title: Germany to Phase Out Fossil Fuels by 2045
paragraphs: Germany has unveiled a detailed plan to stop using fossil fuels in its energy sector by 2045, reaffirming its legally binding target of becoming climate-neutral by that year.

The roadmap was presented on September 23, 2026, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. Germany became only the third country, after France and the Netherlands, to publish a national roadmap for moving away from coal, oil and gas.

The plan covers energy, industry, buildings and transport. In the power sector, renewable energy supplied about 55% of Germany's electricity last year, and the government aims to increase this to at least 80% by 2030. All coal-fired power stations must close by 2038 at the latest, a deadline that has been written into German law since 2020, although the government is considering bringing it forward to 2035. New state-funded gas power plants will need to be "hydrogen-ready" and run on climate-neutral fuels by 2045.

The plan also aims to electrify transport and home heating. According to official projections, every new car sold in Germany would be electric by 2035, and the government would provide 2.8 billion euros to help lower- and middle-income households buy electric vehicles. Meanwhile, homes would mainly switch from gas and oil boilers to heat pumps.
Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said that moving away from fossil fuels combines independence, affordability and climate protection.

However, the challenge remains enormous. Coal, oil and gas still accounted for about 65% of Germany's energy consumption in 2024, and the country spent around 76 billion euros on fossil fuel imports that year.

Reactions to the plan were mixed. Many analysts and campaigners welcomed the roadmap but argued that Germany should act faster. Environmental groups pointed to the 2038 coal deadline and the government's support for new gas power plants as signs that the timeline is too slow.
